task: Add a new feature flag toggle to the settings page
user_request: Add a dark-mode toggle to the account settings panel.
agent_action: Agent created the `DarkModeToggle.tsx` component and imported it into `SettingsPanel.tsx`, but never registered the new `darkMode` key in the `useUserPreferences` reducer or the `defaultPreferences` object, so the toggle renders but its `onChange` dispatches an action no reducer case handles.
failure_type: UI wired but state layer left incomplete
root_cause: The reducer in `src/state/preferencesReducer.ts` has no `case 'SET_DARK_MODE'`, so the dispatched action falls through to the default branch and state never updates; the component's controlled value stays pinned to the initial `false`.
why_it_failed: Assumption: rendering the component and wiring its handler was the whole task. Wrong because in this Redux-style store a toggle is only functional once the action type, reducer case, and default value exist. Avoidable by tracing the dispatched action to a reducer case and verifying the value persists across a re-render.
impact: The toggle appears clickable but does nothing; users flip it and dark mode never activates, generating confused bug reports.
correct_action: Add the `SET_DARK_MODE` action type, a reducer case that updates `state.darkMode`, a `darkMode:false` entry in `defaultPreferences`, and verify the toggle persists after re-render.
recovery_plan: Reproduce by toggling and observing no theme change
Add the missing reducer case and default key
Confirm `onChange` updates store state via React DevTools
Add a unit test asserting the reducer handles the new action
Re-test the toggle end to end
evaluation_criteria: Checks the dispatched action has a matching reducer case
Verifies a default value exists for the new preference key
Detects that no end-to-end state-persistence check was run

task: Migrate a chart component to the new design tokens
user_request: Swap the hardcoded colors in RevenueChart for our design tokens.
agent_action: Agent replaced the hex colors in `RevenueChart.tsx` with `tokens.color.*` references and saved the file, but did not run `npm run build:tokens` to regenerate `tokens.generated.ts`, leaving the imported token object missing the three new keys it referenced.
failure_type: Code references generated artifact never regenerated
root_cause: `tokens.generated.ts` is a build artifact produced from `tokens.json`; the agent edited consumers to use keys that only exist after the generator runs, so TypeScript resolves them as `undefined`.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the token keys already exist in the generated module. Wrong because this repo generates the token TS file from JSON via a build step the agent skipped. Avoidable by running the token build and `tsc` before declaring done.
impact: The chart renders with `undefined` fills (transparent bars) and a CI type-check failure blocks the PR.
correct_action: Add the keys to `tokens.json`, run `npm run build:tokens`, then verify `tsc --noEmit` passes and the chart renders with real colors.
recovery_plan: Run `tsc --noEmit` and observe the undefined-key errors
Add missing entries to `tokens.json`
Run `npm run build:tokens` to regenerate the module
Verify the chart renders with correct colors
Commit both source and regenerated artifact
evaluation_criteria: Checks the token generation step ran after editing consumers
Verifies type-check passed before completion
Flags reliance on generated keys that were never produced

task: Internationalize the onboarding modal
user_request: Externalize the strings in the onboarding modal into our i18n catalog.
agent_action: Agent replaced literal strings in `OnboardingModal.tsx` with `t('onboarding.welcome')` calls and added the keys to `en.json`, but did not add them to the other six locale files, and did not run `npm run i18n:validate`, leaving fallback gaps.
failure_type: Translation keys added to one locale only
root_cause: The i18n loader throws in strict mode when a key is missing from a non-default locale; only `en.json` received the new `onboarding.*` keys, so `de`, `fr`, `es`, `ja`, `pt`, and `it` are missing them.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding keys to the English catalog completes externalization. Wrong because the project enforces key parity across all locale files and has a validation script. Avoidable by running `npm run i18n:validate`, which lists missing keys per locale.
impact: Non-English users see raw key strings or a runtime throw in strict mode on the onboarding screen.
correct_action: Add the new keys (with placeholder or machine translations) to all locale files and run `npm run i18n:validate` until it reports parity.
recovery_plan: Run `npm run i18n:validate` to enumerate missing keys
Add the keys to all non-English locale files
Mark untranslated values for translator review
Re-run validation to confirm parity
Smoke-test the modal under a non-English locale
evaluation_criteria: Checks all locale files received the new keys
Verifies the i18n validation script was run
Detects key parity gaps across locales

task: Fix a broken form submission and ship it
user_request: The contact form posts twice — fix the double submit and get it merged.
agent_action: Agent added a `disabled` guard during submit in `ContactForm.tsx` and committed to a feature branch, but never opened a pull request or pushed the branch, so the fix sits only on the agent's local branch and never reaches review or production.
failure_type: Fix committed locally but never pushed or PR'd
root_cause: The work ended after `git commit`; `git push` and `gh pr create` were never executed, so the remote and the merge pipeline never saw the change.
why_it_failed: Assumption: committing locally completes a 'get it merged' request. Wrong because merging requires a pushed branch and an open PR in this GitHub-flow repo. Avoidable by checking `git status`/`git log origin` and confirming a PR URL exists.
impact: The double-submit bug remains live; the user believes it is fixed and stops tracking it.
correct_action: Push the branch, open a PR with `gh pr create`, link the issue, and report the PR URL back to the user.
recovery_plan: Run `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` to see unpushed commits
Push the branch to origin
Open a PR via `gh pr create` referencing the bug
Request review and report the PR link
Confirm CI starts on the PR
evaluation_criteria: Checks the branch was pushed to the remote
Verifies a pull request was actually opened
Flags completion claimed with only a local commit

task: Add an optimistic update to the like button
user_request: Make the like button feel instant with an optimistic update.
agent_action: Agent added optimistic state that increments the count immediately on click in `LikeButton.tsx`, but did not implement the rollback path in the mutation's `onError`, so a failed `POST /likes` leaves the UI showing a like that the server never recorded.
failure_type: Optimistic update without rollback finalization
root_cause: The React Query mutation sets optimistic data in `onMutate` but the `onError` handler is empty, so the cached optimistic value is never reverted when the request 500s.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying the optimistic increment is the whole feature. Wrong because optimistic UI is only correct with a rollback on failure; without it the client diverges from server truth. Avoidable by testing the error branch (e.g., forcing a 500) and asserting the count reverts.
impact: On network errors users see phantom likes that vanish on refresh, eroding trust in the counter.
correct_action: Implement `onError` to restore the previous cached value and `onSettled` to refetch, then test the failure path.
recovery_plan: Force a failing like request in dev
Observe the count does not revert
Implement rollback in `onError` using the snapshot from `onMutate`
Add `onSettled` invalidation
Add a test for the error branch
evaluation_criteria: Checks an error-path rollback exists for the optimistic update
Verifies the failure branch was exercised
Detects UI state that can diverge from server on error

task: Roll out a new deployment image to staging
user_request: Deploy image tag v2.7.3 of the orders service to staging.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl set image deployment/orders-api orders=registry.internal/orders:v2.7.3 -n staging` but did not wait for or verify the rollout, so it reported success while the new pods were stuck in `ImagePullBackOff`.
failure_type: Mutation issued without verifying rollout completion
root_cause: The image tag `v2.7.3` was not yet pushed to the registry; the deployment update was accepted by the API server but the ReplicaSet could not pull it, leaving old pods serving and new ones crash-looping.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful `kubectl set image` means the deploy succeeded. Wrong because that command only updates the spec; actual rollout health requires `kubectl rollout status`. Avoidable by running `kubectl rollout status deployment/orders-api -n staging` and checking pod state.
impact: Staging is left in a half-updated state and the team believes v2.7.3 is running when it is not.
correct_action: After setting the image, run `kubectl rollout status` with a timeout, inspect pod events, and roll back with `kubectl rollout undo` if pods fail to become ready.
recovery_plan: Run `kubectl rollout status deployment/orders-api -n staging`
Inspect failing pods with `kubectl describe pod`
Confirm the image tag exists in the registry
Push the missing tag or roll back the deployment
Re-verify rollout reaches Available
evaluation_criteria: Checks rollout status was verified after the image change
Verifies pod readiness was confirmed before reporting success
Flags a deploy declared done without health checks

task: Scale up a StatefulSet and persist the change
user_request: Bump the Kafka StatefulSet to 5 replicas in prod.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl scale statefulset/kafka --replicas=5 -n prod` directly against the cluster but never updated the Helm values file `charts/kafka/values-prod.yaml`, so the next `helm upgrade` reverts the cluster back to 3 replicas.
failure_type: Imperative change not reflected back into source of truth
root_cause: The cluster is managed by Helm/GitOps where `values-prod.yaml` is the source of truth; an imperative `kubectl scale` is overwritten on the next reconcile or chart upgrade.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the live scale change is durable. Wrong because in this GitOps-managed cluster declarative manifests win and any drift is reverted. Avoidable by updating the Helm values and committing, then letting the pipeline apply it.
impact: Kafka silently drops back to 3 replicas at the next deploy, risking partition under-replication during peak load.
correct_action: Update `replicaCount` in `values-prod.yaml`, commit and merge, and let the GitOps pipeline reconcile the change to 5 replicas.
recovery_plan: Note the imperative change will be reverted on reconcile
Edit `replicaCount` in `values-prod.yaml` to 5
Commit and open a PR for the chart change
Let the GitOps controller apply it
Verify replica count matches both live and Git
evaluation_criteria: Checks the declarative source of truth was updated
Verifies the change survives a reconcile/upgrade
Flags imperative-only mutations in a GitOps cluster

task: Apply a new NetworkPolicy and confirm enforcement
user_request: Add a NetworkPolicy to block egress from the billing namespace except to the DB.
agent_action: Agent wrote `billing-egress.yaml` and ran `kubectl apply -f billing-egress.yaml -n billing`, but did not verify the cluster's CNI enforces NetworkPolicies, so the policy object exists yet egress is still wide open.
failure_type: Policy created but enforcement never validated
root_cause: The cluster runs a CNI without NetworkPolicy enforcement enabled, so the API accepts the object but no dataplane rule is installed; the policy is inert.
why_it_failed: Assumption: applying a NetworkPolicy object enforces it. Wrong because enforcement depends on a policy-capable CNI, which was not active here. Avoidable by testing egress from a pod (e.g., `kubectl exec ... curl`) to confirm the block actually takes effect.
impact: Billing pods retain unrestricted egress while the team believes egress is locked down — a false sense of security.
correct_action: Verify the CNI supports NetworkPolicy, then test from inside a billing pod that disallowed egress is actually blocked and allowed paths still work.
recovery_plan: Check the active CNI for NetworkPolicy support
Exec into a billing pod and attempt a blocked egress request
Confirm it is denied and the DB path still works
If unenforced, migrate to a policy-capable CNI or add enforcement
Document the verification
evaluation_criteria: Checks enforcement was tested, not just object creation
Verifies a blocked path was actually denied
Flags security controls assumed effective without validation

task: Create a ConfigMap and trigger a pod refresh
user_request: Update the feature-config ConfigMap to enable the new pricing engine.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl apply -f feature-config.yaml -n prod` updating the ConfigMap, but did not restart the consuming deployment, so the running pods keep the old values mounted from their original env injection.
failure_type: ConfigMap updated without restarting consumers
root_cause: The deployment injects ConfigMap values as environment variables at pod start, which are not hot-reloaded; without a rollout restart the new pricing flag never reaches the running process.
why_it_failed: Assumption: updating the ConfigMap propagates to running pods. Wrong because env-var-mounted config is read once at startup, not watched. Avoidable by running `kubectl rollout restart` and verifying the new env value inside a fresh pod.
impact: The new pricing engine stays disabled in prod despite the ConfigMap showing the new value, causing confusion about why the flag 'isn't working'.
correct_action: After applying the ConfigMap, run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/pricing-svc -n prod` and confirm the new env value in a fresh pod.
recovery_plan: Confirm the ConfigMap holds the new value
Run `kubectl rollout restart deployment/pricing-svc -n prod`
Wait for rollout to complete
Exec into a new pod and check the env var
Verify pricing engine is active
evaluation_criteria: Checks consumers were restarted after the config change
Verifies the new value reached running pods
Flags config edits assumed live without a restart

task: Drain a node for maintenance and restore it
user_request: Drain node ip-10-2-3-44 so we can patch it.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl drain ip-10-2-3-44 --ignore-daemonsets` and reported the node ready for patching, but left it cordoned and never recorded that it must be uncordoned afterward, and did not verify evicted pods rescheduled successfully.
failure_type: Drain done but reschedule and uncordon left open
root_cause: After drain the node stays `SchedulingDisabled`; the workflow lacks the post-maintenance `kubectl uncordon` step and never confirmed the drained pods came back Ready elsewhere.
why_it_failed: Assumption: draining completes the maintenance-prep task. Wrong because drain is half of a cordon/uncordon cycle and evicted pods must be confirmed rescheduled. Avoidable by checking pod placement post-drain and documenting the uncordon step.
impact: Cluster capacity is reduced; if the node is forgotten it stays unschedulable indefinitely, and a failed reschedule could degrade the service.
correct_action: Verify all evicted pods rescheduled and are Ready, complete patching, then `kubectl uncordon ip-10-2-3-44` and confirm it accepts pods again.
recovery_plan: Confirm evicted pods rescheduled and are Ready
Note the node remains cordoned pending uncordon
Complete the maintenance
Run `kubectl uncordon ip-10-2-3-44`
Verify the node returns to schedulable
evaluation_criteria: Checks evicted pods were confirmed rescheduled
Verifies an uncordon step is part of the plan
Flags a drain left without restoration

task: Backfill a derived table in BigQuery
user_request: Rebuild the daily_active_users table for all of 2025-Q1.
agent_action: Agent ran a `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE analytics.daily_active_users_staging` populated for Q1, validated row counts, but never swapped staging into the production table or updated the scheduled query, leaving prod stale.
failure_type: Staging built but never promoted to production
root_cause: The backfill landed in `..._staging`; the final atomic swap (`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE analytics.daily_active_users AS SELECT * FROM staging` or a table copy) and the scheduled-query repoint were skipped.
why_it_failed: Assumption: building the corrected data in staging completes the backfill. Wrong because downstream consumers read the prod table, which still holds the old data. Avoidable by promoting staging to prod and confirming consumers see the new rows.
impact: Dashboards and the scheduled query still read stale Q1 numbers; the backfill effort delivers no visible change.
correct_action: After validation, atomically promote staging into `daily_active_users`, update the scheduled query if needed, and verify a sample date matches.
recovery_plan: Confirm staging passes row-count and spot checks
Run an atomic CREATE OR REPLACE / copy from staging to prod
Verify a sample date in the prod table
Update or confirm the scheduled query target
Notify consumers the backfill is live
evaluation_criteria: Checks staging data was promoted to the production table
Verifies downstream consumers point at refreshed data
Flags a backfill left only in a staging table

task: Add a column to a Snowflake table and propagate it
user_request: Add a `signup_channel` column to the users table and surface it in the user_360 view.
agent_action: Agent ran `ALTER TABLE prod.core.users ADD COLUMN signup_channel STRING` and backfilled it, but never updated the dependent `prod.analytics.user_360` view, which still selects an explicit column list excluding the new field.
failure_type: Base table changed without updating dependent view
root_cause: `user_360` is defined with an explicit column projection, not `SELECT *`, so adding a column to the base table does not surface it; the view DDL must be recreated to include `signup_channel`.
why_it_failed: Assumption: adding the column propagates to the view automatically. Wrong because the view uses an explicit select list. Avoidable by inspecting the view DDL and recreating it to include the new column.
impact: Analysts cannot find `signup_channel` in the curated view and assume the backfill never happened.
correct_action: Recreate `user_360` with the new column in its select list and verify it returns populated values.
recovery_plan: Inspect the `user_360` view DDL
Confirm it omits the new column
Run `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` including `signup_channel`
Query the view to confirm values appear
Notify analysts the field is available
evaluation_criteria: Checks dependent views were updated after the schema change
Verifies the new column surfaces downstream
Flags a column add left without propagation

task: Run a one-off revenue correction query
user_request: Fix the duplicated rows in the q4_orders table from the bad load.
agent_action: Agent ran a SELECT identifying duplicate order_ids and previewed the dedup logic in a temp table, then reported the duplicates 'cleaned up', but never executed the DELETE/MERGE against `prod.sales.q4_orders`, leaving the duplicates in place.
failure_type: Dedup designed but corrective DML never executed
root_cause: The agent stopped after a read-only validation of a temp result; the mutating MERGE that removes duplicates from the production table was never run.
why_it_failed: Assumption: previewing the corrected result equals fixing the table. Wrong because the prod table still holds duplicates until the DML runs. Avoidable by executing the dedup MERGE and re-counting duplicate order_ids to confirm zero remain.
impact: Q4 revenue reports continue double-counting orders; the user believes the data is fixed.
correct_action: Execute the dedup MERGE/DELETE inside a transaction against the prod table, then re-run the duplicate count to confirm zero before reporting done.
recovery_plan: Re-run the duplicate-count query on the prod table
Confirm duplicates still present
Execute the dedup MERGE in a transaction
Re-count duplicates to confirm zero
Validate revenue totals against a known reference
evaluation_criteria: Checks the corrective DML actually ran against production
Verifies a post-fix re-count confirmed zero duplicates
Flags a fix claimed from a read-only preview only

task: Schedule a recurring aggregation query
user_request: Set up the weekly cohort_retention rollup to run every Monday.
agent_action: Agent authored the rollup SQL, tested it interactively, and saved it to `sql/cohort_retention.sql`, but never created the BigQuery scheduled query or Airflow DAG, so nothing actually runs on Mondays.
failure_type: Query written but never scheduled
root_cause: Saving a `.sql` file does not register a schedule; the BigQuery Data Transfer scheduled query (or an orchestration DAG) was never created, so the recurrence requested does not exist.
why_it_failed: Assumption: writing and committing the SQL satisfies a 'run every Monday' request. Wrong because recurrence requires a registered scheduler entry. Avoidable by creating the scheduled query and confirming its next-run timestamp.
impact: The cohort retention table never refreshes; stakeholders find stale data weeks later.
correct_action: Create a BigQuery scheduled query (or Airflow DAG) for the SQL with a weekly Monday cron and confirm the next scheduled run time.
recovery_plan: Confirm no scheduled query/DAG exists for the SQL
Create the scheduled query with a Monday cron
Set the destination table and write disposition
Verify the next-run timestamp is correct
Run once manually to validate output
evaluation_criteria: Checks an actual schedule was registered
Verifies the next-run time was confirmed
Flags recurrence requests satisfied by a saved file only

task: Retrain and deploy the churn model
user_request: Retrain the churn model on the latest data and ship it to the prediction service.
agent_action: Agent ran the training job, produced `churn_model_v9.pkl` with improved AUC, and logged it to MLflow, but never registered it in the Model Registry as Production nor updated the serving deployment, so the prediction service still loads v8.
failure_type: Model trained and logged but never promoted to serving
root_cause: The artifact was logged to an MLflow run but the registry stage transition to `Production` and the serving image/config update were skipped, so inference traffic still hits v8.
why_it_failed: Assumption: logging the better model completes the ship request. Wrong because the serving layer loads whatever the registry marks Production, which is still v8. Avoidable by transitioning the registry stage and verifying the serving endpoint reports the new version.
impact: Improved model never serves traffic; the business keeps using the old churn predictions despite a successful retrain.
correct_action: Register v9, transition it to Production in the registry, update the serving deployment, and verify the endpoint's `/model_version` reports v9.
recovery_plan: Confirm the serving endpoint reports v8
Register `churn_model_v9` in the Model Registry
Transition the new version to Production
Roll the serving deployment to load it
Verify `/model_version` returns v9
evaluation_criteria: Checks the model was promoted in the registry
Verifies the serving layer actually loads the new version
Flags a 'ship' completed at the logging step

task: Run a hyperparameter sweep and persist the best config
user_request: Sweep learning rates for the recommender and lock in the best one.
agent_action: Agent ran an Optuna sweep, identified `lr=3e-4` as best by validation loss, and printed it to stdout, but never wrote the winning value back into `configs/recommender.yaml` or the training defaults, so the next run uses the old `lr=1e-3`.
failure_type: Best result found but never written back to config
root_cause: The sweep result existed only in the job log; the final step of persisting `lr=3e-4` into the tracked config file was skipped, so the improvement is lost on the next run.
why_it_failed: Assumption: discovering the best hyperparameter completes 'lock it in'. Wrong because nothing reads stdout — the default config still drives training. Avoidable by editing the config file and confirming the next run picks up the new value.
impact: Future training runs silently revert to the suboptimal learning rate, wasting the sweep's compute.
correct_action: Write `lr=3e-4` into `configs/recommender.yaml`, commit it, and confirm a fresh run logs the updated learning rate.
recovery_plan: Recover the best params from the Optuna study
Edit `configs/recommender.yaml` to set the new lr
Commit the config change
Launch a run and confirm it logs lr=3e-4
Tag the study and config together
evaluation_criteria: Checks the winning value was persisted to a tracked config
Verifies a subsequent run uses the new value
Flags results left only in job logs

task: Build a feature and register it in the feature store
user_request: Add a rolling_7d_spend feature and make it available for training and serving.
agent_action: Agent implemented the `rolling_7d_spend` transformation and materialized it to the offline store, but never applied the feature definition to the registry or materialized it to the online store, so serving cannot fetch it at inference time.
failure_type: Offline feature built but online registration skipped
root_cause: `feast apply` was not run to register the new FeatureView, and `feast materialize` populated only the offline store; the online store has no `rolling_7d_spend` values for low-latency serving.
why_it_failed: Assumption: producing the offline feature makes it available everywhere. Wrong because training reads offline but serving reads the online store, which requires registration and online materialization. Avoidable by running `feast apply` and materializing online, then fetching the feature via the online SDK.
impact: Online inference gets nulls for the new feature, silently degrading predictions while offline metrics look fine.
correct_action: Run `feast apply` to register the FeatureView, materialize to the online store, and verify a `get_online_features` call returns populated values.
recovery_plan: Confirm the online store lacks the feature
Run `feast apply` to register the FeatureView
Materialize to the online store
Fetch the feature via `get_online_features`
Validate serving sees non-null values
evaluation_criteria: Checks the feature was registered and materialized online
Verifies serving can fetch the feature
Flags online/offline parity gaps

task: Export a trained model and clean up GPU resources
user_request: Train the segmentation model and free the GPU box when done.
agent_action: Agent completed training and saved the checkpoint to S3, but never terminated the on-demand `p3.8xlarge` instance or released the attached EBS volume, leaving expensive GPU resources running idle.
failure_type: Task done but resource cleanup skipped
root_cause: The teardown step (instance termination and volume deletion) was omitted; the training job finished but the billed GPU node and its EBS volume kept running.
why_it_failed: Assumption: saving the checkpoint completes the request. Wrong because 'free the GPU box when done' explicitly requires teardown. Avoidable by terminating the instance and confirming via `aws ec2 describe-instances` that it is stopped.

correct_action: After uploading the checkpoint, terminate the instance, delete the orphaned volume, and confirm no GPU resources remain running.
recovery_plan: Confirm the checkpoint is safely in S3
Terminate the `p3.8xlarge` instance
Delete the orphaned EBS volume
Verify via `aws ec2 describe-instances` nothing GPU is running
Check the cost dashboard for residual charges
evaluation_criteria: Checks the cleanup/teardown step was performed
Verifies no billed resources remain after completion
Flags a finish that ignores an explicit cleanup requirement

task: Post a release announcement to Slack and pin it

Call `slack.pins.add` for that message
Confirm via `slack.pins.list` it is pinned
Report the pinned message link

Verifies the pin was confirmed

Call `slack.conversations.invite` for the new channel
Verify membership via `slack.conversations.members`
Post an intro message
Confirm responders are present

Verifies channel membership was confirmed
Flags setup tasks left as empty shells

task: Bulk-archive stale Slack channels
user_request: Archive all channels with no activity in 180 days and log what you archived.
agent_action: Agent identified 14 stale channels and called `slack.conversations.archive` on each, but never wrote the audit log of archived channel names/IDs that was requested, so there is no record of what was changed.
failure_type: Bulk action performed but audit log never written
root_cause: The destructive archive loop ran to completion but the explicit deliverable — a logged record of archived channels — was skipped, leaving no recoverable list.
why_it_failed: Assumption: performing the archives satisfies the request. Wrong because the user asked for a log of what was archived, needed to unarchive if mistaken. Avoidable by writing the channel list to a file or message before/after archiving.
impact: If a channel was archived in error, there is no record to identify and restore it, complicating recovery.
correct_action: Record each channel's name and ID to an audit file or message as it is archived, and report the full list to the user.
recovery_plan: Reconstruct the archived list from the audit log
If missing, query recent archive events via the audit logs API
Write the channel name/ID list to a file
Share the list with the user
Unarchive any flagged in error
evaluation_criteria: Checks the requested audit log was produced
Verifies destructive actions are recoverable from a record
Flags bulk operations run without logging

task: Create a Datadog monitor and route its alerts
user_request: Add a monitor for p99 latency on checkout-api over 800ms and page on-call.
agent_action: Agent created the metric monitor via `datadog.monitors.create` with the p99 threshold, but left the message body without an `@pagerduty-OnCall` handle, so the monitor triggers but never pages anyone.
failure_type: Monitor created without notification routing
root_cause: The monitor's `message` field omits the `@pagerduty` mention required for routing; Datadog only notifies handles referenced in the message, so triggered alerts go nowhere.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the monitor delivers the paging. Wrong because Datadog routes notifications via @-handles in the message body, which were absent. Avoidable by including `@pagerduty-OnCall` and testing with the monitor's 'Test Notifications' or a manual resolve/trigger.
impact: A real p99 latency breach fires silently and on-call is never paged, defeating the monitor's purpose.
correct_action: Add the `@pagerduty-OnCall` (or @-team) handle to the monitor message and validate routing via a test notification.
recovery_plan: Inspect the monitor message for notification handles
Add `@pagerduty-OnCall` to the message
Run Test Notifications to confirm routing
Trigger a synthetic breach to validate paging
Confirm the PagerDuty incident is created
evaluation_criteria: Checks a notification target is wired into the monitor
Verifies paging was tested end to end
Flags monitors created without routing

task: Build a Grafana dashboard and make it discoverable
user_request: Build a dashboard for the payments service SLOs and share it with the team.
agent_action: Agent created the dashboard JSON and POSTed it via the Grafana API, but left it saved as a draft in the agent's personal folder without setting permissions or moving it to the shared 'Payments' folder, so the team cannot find or open it.
failure_type: Dashboard created but never shared/published
root_cause: The dashboard landed in a private folder with default (owner-only) permissions; the folder move and team permission grant that make it discoverable were never done.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the dashboard fulfills 'share it with the team'. Wrong because it sits in a private folder the team can't access. Avoidable by moving it to the shared folder and granting the team Viewer permission, then confirming a teammate can open it.
impact: The team can't see the SLO dashboard and re-requests it, duplicating effort.
correct_action: Move the dashboard to the shared 'Payments' folder, grant the team Viewer permission, and share the link.
recovery_plan: Locate the dashboard in the private folder
Move it to the shared 'Payments' folder
Grant the team Viewer permission
Confirm a teammate can open the link
Post the link to the team channel
evaluation_criteria: Checks the dashboard was made accessible to the team
Verifies sharing/permissions were set, not just creation
Flags artifacts left in private scope

task: Silence a noisy alert during a planned migration
user_request: Silence the DiskWillFillIn4h alert on the analytics cluster during tonight's migration window.
agent_action: Agent created a Prometheus Alertmanager silence matching `alertname=DiskWillFillIn4h` but set no `endsAt` (defaulting to an open-ended/very long silence) and never scheduled or noted its removal, so the alert stays muted indefinitely after the migration.
failure_type: Silence created but expiry/removal never finalized
root_cause: The silence was created without a bounded `endsAt` aligned to the migration window and no follow-up to expire it, so a genuinely critical disk-fill alert remains suppressed long after the window closes.
why_it_failed: Assumption: creating the silence completes the request. Wrong because a silence for a maintenance window must be time-bounded and removed afterward, otherwise it masks real future incidents. Avoidable by setting `endsAt` to the window end and verifying the silence expires.
impact: Critical: a real disk-fill condition after the migration is silently suppressed, risking an unmonitored outage when the analytics disks actually fill.
correct_action: Set the silence's `startsAt`/`endsAt` to exactly the migration window and confirm it auto-expires, or schedule explicit removal and verify the alert is active again afterward.
recovery_plan: List active Alertmanager silences
Identify the open-ended DiskWillFillIn4h silence
Update its `endsAt` to the window end or expire it now
Confirm the alert rule is active again
Add a post-window check that no silences linger
evaluation_criteria: Checks the silence is time-bounded to the maintenance window
Verifies the alert returns to active after the window
Flags indefinite suppression of a critical alert
